newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PSC says patrol vessel project still on.
newsitem.headline: PSC says patrol vessel project still on.

text.p: PSC Industries Bhd said on Monday it was not aware of any postponement to its multi-billlion ringgit offshore patrol vessel project.

"As far as we are concerned, the project is still on," PSC chairman Amin Shah Omar Shah told reporters, in response to a news report that the project has been put on hold indefinitely by the government.

The Sun newspaper, quoting a "well-informed source", said on Monday the government decided on the postponement after studying the financial implications of the project and its adverse impact on the country's current account deficit.
"The news is quite a surprise to us...," Amin Shah said.
PSC on Monday suspended its stock in order to clarify on the report.
PSC shares, which fell 1.50 ringgit to 33.25 ringgit on Monday before the suspension, should be requoted on Thursday, said Amin Shah.
The project is an integral part of the privatisation of Naval Dockyard Sdn Bhd which controls the naval dockyard in northern coastal town of Lumut.
Under the project, Naval Dockyard is to build 27 offshore patrol vessels for the Malaysian navy over 15 years as a cost of 5.6 billion ringgit.
Naval Dockyard is 40 percent owned by Penang Shipyard and Construction Sdn Bhd, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of PSC.
